new_note: Matthew 10:18 — *And ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.* The youth confessing before the tyrant that he suffers for defending the Law of Elohim is the standing before kings as a testimony that the Messiah foretold.

Deuteronomy 30:16 — *I command thee this day to love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply.* Their resolve to walk in obedience to the Law and take Moses as counsellor is the walking in his ways that Moses commanded for life.

1 John 3:16 — *Hereby perceive we the love of Elohim (God), because he laid down his life for us: and we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren* — the laying down of life for one's brethren that the seven enacted to the death, brotherly love bred under the Law.

Daniel 12:2 — *and many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life* — the resurrection of the just, the *pure and immortal souls* the sons of Abraham received from Elohim.

Revelation 6:12 — *And I beheld when he had opened the sixth seal, and, lo, there was a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon became as blood.* The hidden light of the luminaries is John's sun that turns black as sackcloth, and blood-red moon at the great judgment.

1 Corinthians 15:22 — *For as in Adam all die, even so in Messiah (Christ) shall all be made alive.* Raising Adam with every man of his seed is Paul's word that in Adam all die and in Messiah all are made alive — the same root and the same harvest.

Ephesians 5:31 — *For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall be joined unto his wife, and they two shall be one flesh.* Eve's plea that they not be separated is Paul's one-flesh union carried from Genesis.

Hebrews 9:14 — *the blood of Messiah (Christ), who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to Elohim (God), purge your conscience from dead works* — the blood that truly purifies, which Eleazar's *make my blood their purification* pointed toward.

Isaiah 53:10 — *when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days* — the soul given as an offering for sin, which the martyr's surrendered soul only pointed toward.

Isaiah 53:5 — *he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed* — the Suffering Servant whose pattern Eleazar's blood-plea dimly reflects, a pattern that waited for its fulfilment.

Isaiah 53:5 — *But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed* — the Suffering Servant whose wounded blood truly delivers, which the martyrs' death only pointed toward.

Isaiah 53:12 — *he hath poured out his soul unto death... and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors* — the One who pours out his soul and bears the nation's sin, the one whom the martyrs' blood foreshadows.

Hebrews 9:14 — *the blood of Messiah, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to Elohim, purge your conscience from dead works* — the blood that truly cleanses the people, which the martyrs' blood only pointed toward.

Leviticus 19:9 — *And when ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest.* To be one who "refrains from gleaning his stubbles" is to obey the law of the corners and the gleanings left for the poor.
flag: Quote now matches live 4 Maccabees 2:2 wording ('refrains from gleaning his stubbles').

new_note: Deuteronomy 30:19 — *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.* The Law that Elohim (God) gave "to the mind," so that a man may reign over a kingdom that is temperate and just, is the choice of life Moses sets before Israel.
